title: Finite modular energy and entropy balance

items.title: Finite matrix entropy derivative at a faithful state
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with a fixed orthonormal basis, let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, and let $t_0\in J$. Suppose $A:J\to\operatorname{End}(H)$ has real and imaginary matrix entries in the fixed basis differentiable at $t_0$ and is self-adjoint with strictly positive eigenvalues on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq J$ of $t_0$. Let $\operatorname{tr}$ be the finite-dimensional trace, and let $\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup_{\|v\|=1}\|Tv\|$ be the operator norm. For $t\in U$, define $\log A(t)$ by applying the natural logarithm to the eigenvalues of $A(t)$ in its spectral decomposition and set $G:U\to\mathbb R$ by $G(t):=\operatorname{tr}(A(t)\log A(t))$. Then $G$ is differentiable at $t_0$ and

$$G'(t_0)=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(A'(t_0)(\log A(t_0)+I_H)\right),$$

where $I_H$ is the identity endomorphism of $H$ and $A'(t_0)$ is obtained by differentiating the matrix entries in the fixed basis.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted complete book manuscript, §5.2.1
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, complete book manuscript, §11.1

items.title: Finite relative entropy equals modular energy minus entropy
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Let $\rho,\sigma:H\to H$ be self-adjoint linear maps with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one, and suppose every eigenvalue of $\sigma$ is strictly positive. Define $K_\sigma:=-\log\sigma$ by spectral calculus, and for any self-adjoint $\tau:H\to H$ with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one define $s(\tau):=-\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\tau)=-\sum_{\lambda_j(\tau)>0}\lambda_j(\tau)\log\lambda_j(\tau)$, with the zero-eigenvalue term $0\log0:=0$ and natural logarithms, so the entropy is in nats. Define the modular-energy difference relative to $\sigma$ by $\Delta_K(\rho,\sigma):=\operatorname{tr}((\rho-\sigma)K_\sigma)$. Then

$$D(\rho\|\sigma)=\Delta_K(\rho,\sigma)-(s(\rho)-s(\sigma)).$$

For any nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_A,H_B$ with $H=H_A\otimes H_B$, partial tracing both states over $H_B$ cannot increase relative entropy:

$$D(\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho\|\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\sigma)\le D(\rho\|\sigma).$$

The identity and inequality are finite-dimensional mathematical statements; no Hamiltonian, physical energy, physical units, continuum limit, or gravitational entropy is assumed.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted complete book manuscript, §§5.2.1–5.2.3
Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, §2.5
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, complete book manuscript, §§11.1 and 11.8

items.title: Finite-dimensional entropy first variation at a faithful state
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$. Let $\rho:I\to\operatorname{End}(H)$ be a path whose real and imaginary matrix entries are continuously differentiable on $I$, such that each $\rho(\varepsilon)$ is self-adjoint with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one. Suppose $\rho(0)=\sigma$ and every eigenvalue of $\sigma$ is strictly positive. Define $K_\sigma:=-\log\sigma$ by spectral calculus and let $s(\tau):=-\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\tau)$ with the finite spectral convention $0\log0:=0$. Then

$$\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}s(\rho(\varepsilon))\right|_{\varepsilon=0}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho'(0)K_\sigma).$$

If, in addition, the real and imaginary matrix entries of $\rho$ are twice continuously differentiable on $I$, then the finite relative entropy $D(\rho(\varepsilon)\|\sigma)$ has zero first derivative at $\varepsilon=0$. These are finite-dimensional mathematical statements and make no continuum or gravitational claim.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted complete book manuscript, §5.2.1
Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, §2.5
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, complete book manuscript, §§11.1 and 11.8

title: Finite modular energy and entropy balance — Examples

items.title: Two-level entropy first variation
items.statement:
On $H=\mathbb C^2$ with its standard inner product and standard basis, fix $p\in(0,1)$ and set $\sigma:=\operatorname{diag}(p,1-p)$. For $|\varepsilon|<\min\{p,1-p\}$ define $\rho(\varepsilon):=\operatorname{diag}(p+\varepsilon,1-p-\varepsilon)$ and $s(\rho(\varepsilon)):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\varepsilon)\log\rho(\varepsilon))$. Then every $\rho(\varepsilon)$ is a positive-definite density matrix, $\rho(0)=\sigma$, and

$$\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}s(\rho(\varepsilon))\right|_{\varepsilon=0}=\log\!\left(\frac{1-p}{p}\right).$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted complete book manuscript, §5.2.1
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, complete book manuscript, §11.1
